title: Andersson 1976: L3-L4 IDP, upright and slow trunk flexion to 45 deg holding 100 N
condition: upright standing then slow flexion to 45 deg (hydrogoniometer at T10) and back, both arms loaded by 100 N

quantity.name: IDP
quantity.definition: absolute in vivo L3-L4 IDP (MPa): mean value in upright standing before/after, and the peak during a slow flexion-extension to 45 deg; needle-tip subminiature transducer of Nachemson & Elfstrom 1970; values as printed (Dreischarf 2016 lists the standing value 0.33 MPa uncorrected, i.e. no -0.25 MPa early-transducer correction)

source.authors: Andersson GBJ, Ortengren R, Nachemson A
source.journal: Spine 1(3):178-185 (Quantitative studies of back loads in lifting)
source.sample: 4 healthy volunteers (3F, 1M), no history of back pain, L3-L4 ('third lumbar disc')
source.citation_note: no DOI found in the PDF; same 4 subjects as the unnamed row '1-4, No LBP history, 29 (26-34) y, 3 f 1 m, 52-69 kg, 169-177 cm, IDP 0.33 MPa' of Dreischarf 2016 Table 1

protocol.summary: Both arms loaded by 100 N (10.2 kg; arm posture not stated, assumed hanging), trunk flexed slowly until a hydrogoniometer at T10 read 45 deg forward flexion, then extended back to upright. IDP rose gradually with flexion and fell on return (text p.181, Table 2).
how_to_simulate: Scale the model to the cohort (3 F / 1 M, 29 y; ~173 cm, ~60 kg = range midpoints)
Hold 10.2 kg (100 N total) in both hands, arms hanging
Upright standing ('before flexion'), then trunk flexion 45 deg (T10 inclination from upright) for the peak
Output L3-L4 compression and flexion; convert with Ghezelbash 2016 Eq. 6 (disc area not reported)

subject_model.source: Andersson 1976 Methods (ranges only; height/weight = range midpoints, means not reported); disc area not reported

protocol.idp_conversion: IDP = -1.556e-2 + 1.255 P + 1.243e-2 th + 3.988e-2 P^2 - 1.212e-2 P th + 1.669e-3 th^2 (MPa), P = F_compression / A_disc (MPa = N/mm2), th = L4-L5 intersegmental flexion from upright standing (deg, + flexion). Source: Ghezelbash et al. 2016 Biomech Model Mechanobiol 15:1699, Eq. 6 (U01 p.10; quadratic fit to the Shirazi-Adl 2006 L4-L5 FE model, R2 0.999, RMSE 0.025 MPa; derived with that model's disc area 1455 mm2, applied with the subject's own area); used again as Eq. 1-2 in Ghezelbash et al. 2020 J Biomech 102:109550 and in the Ghezelbash lab MSK validation. Sensitivity alternative: classical Nachemson factor IDP = F / (0.66 A) (Bruno et al. 2015 J Biomech Eng Eq. 2; Dreischarf 2016 V05 uses F = 0.66 IDP A).
protocol.notes: Parentheses in Table 2 = SEM (n=4); SD = 2 x SEM. 'Before flexion' standing (0.72) exceeds the unloaded standing value 0.33 MPa (Table 1 footnote), consistent with the 100 N already held; load per arm vs total and arm posture are not stated explicitly. Peak = peak during the movement (reached near 45 deg). EMG (Table 2) is raw microvolts and was not extracted (EMG rule). Not extracted: static 400 N pulls (Fig 2, figure-only, posture not quantified), dynamic lifts of 100 N from 45 cm (Table 1: leg lift 1.50, back lift 1.83 MPa peaks; dynamic, posture at peak not given), 50 N held at arm's length (time traces only).

data.x: peak during slow flexion to 45 deg

extraction.uncertainty: values as printed; SD converted from SEM (n=4)
extraction.check_notes: DP column re-read on a 250 dpi render: 0.72 (0.09), 1.68 (0.25), 0.63 (0.06); IAP 0.33/1.60/0.20 kPa not used.

pass_rule.rule: pass if |model - measured| <= max(SD or half-range, 0.26 x measured); pooled over all L4-L5 tasks R2 >= 0.78 with slope 95% CI containing 1 and intercept CI containing 0
pass_rule.source: Ghezelbash lab validation targets tolerance_policy.idp_task / idp_aggregate (CV_pool 0.26 = pooled between-subject CV of Sato 1999's 8 healthy subjects)
